sections.h2: Where is New Windsor and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
New Windsor is a town on the west bank of the Hudson River in eastern Orange County, directly south of the city of Newburgh. The Hudson forms its eastern line, facing Dutchess County, and the town covers 34.08 square miles of land at an elevation of about 512 feet.

It is not one village. The town is a patchwork of hamlets, and a few, such as Rock Tavern and Vails Gate, have their own ZIP codes. Vails Gate sits just south of the city of Newburgh at a historic crossroads, Rock Tavern and Little Britain lie along Route 207 in the west, and Beaver Dam Lake and Firthcliffe Heights are near the southern line. Plum Point, on the river, is a park that opened in 1996.

The Census Bureau counted 27,805 residents in 2020 and estimates 27,844 for July 1, 2025, so the town has held roughly level for five years. That steadiness matters if you are pricing a house: you are selling into a settled suburb, not a boom area.

sections.h2: What is New Windsor's history, and does it affect homes today?
sections.html:
New Windsor was founded by the General Assembly of New York on April 5, 1763. Scottish colonists settled near Moodna Creek in 1685, and the town takes its name from Windsor, England.

The best-known chapter came in October 1782, when the Continental Army built a cantonment of more than 700 huts across about 1,600 acres, housing 6,000 to 8,000 soldiers, women and children. The town later bought a 167-acre tract covering much of the old hut sites. The National Purple Heart Hall of Honor stands on Route 300 in the town, a reminder that the Purple Heart traces back to Washington's Badge of Military Merit.

For a homeowner, history shows up in the housing stock. Clancyville, also called Ducktown, grew in the late 1800s around mills on Quassaick Creek, with small homes enlarged over the years by the Polish, Italian and other immigrant families who built them. Older additions like those are a common source of questions about permits, so check your paperwork before listing.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about homes and households in New Windsor?
sections.html:
New Windsor is mostly a town of owners at middle-range prices for the Hudson Valley. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 73.2 percent, the median home value at $371,900 and median gross rent at $1,606 for 2020 to 2024.

  • Households: 10,981, averaging 2.50 people
  • Median household income: $95,071 in 2024 dollars
  • Persons in poverty: 5.4 percent
  • Mean travel time to work: 37.3 minutes
  • Residents with a bachelor's degree or higher: 37.3 percent

At 37.3 minutes, the average trip to work is longer than in New Rochelle, which fits a town whose main road links are the Thruway and state routes.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve a house in New Windsor?
sections.html:
Four districts cover parts of the town: Newburgh City School District, Washingtonville Central, Cornwall Central and Valley Central, which is based in Montgomery. Which one applies depends on the street, so look up the address instead of assuming.

The district also decides which school tax bill a new owner receives. Public schools inside the town include New Windsor School, Temple Hill School, Vails Gate High Technology Magnet School and Little Britain Elementary School.

When you list or take a cash offer, note the district name for your house on the paperwork you hand the buyer.

sections.h2: How do roads and the airport shape a sale in New Windsor?
sections.html:
The New York State Thruway, Interstate 87, runs north to south through the town, and Route 207 is the main east-west state road. Stewart International Airport sits partly in New Windsor and partly in the town of Newburgh, and a newer entrance on Route 747 connects it straight to the interstates.

Stewart was once an Air Force base. Today it also hosts the New York Air National Guard and a Marine Corps Reserve detachment. More than 8,000 acres of buffer land were acquired around the field when a larger jetport was planned, and many early farms were lost in the process.

Climate is humid continental with four distinct seasons, so roofs, gutters and heating systems get a real workout. A buyer's inspector will look closely at all three.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due in New Windsor, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Property tax bills are mailed in the last week of December and can be paid without penalty through January. The Receiver of Taxes sets the late-payment steps in the table below, and unpaid bills move to the county after April 1.

Payment monthWhat the Town of New Windsor charges
JanuaryNo penalty
February1 percent penalty
MarchAn additional 1 percent plus a $2.00 notice fee
After April 1Unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance for collection

Source: Town of New Windsor Receiver of Taxes page.

The town warns that a USPS postmark now reflects the day mail is processed, not the day it is dropped off, and that a postage-meter mark does not count. If you are selling and a payment is close to the deadline, pay online by e-check or in person at the Receiver of Taxes office. Bills for lenders that hold escrow are sent to the bank, and a seller who refinanced or paid off a mortgage should tell the Receiver's office so the next bill reaches the right person.

sections.h2: How do I deal with STAR, the Assessor and the building department when selling?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's office for exemptions, and the Building Department for permits and occupancy paperwork. The Assessor posted a notice in August 2025: owners who age into Enhanced STAR, or who have an ownership change, no longer file with the assessor. The state notifies local assessors instead, and ownership changes are reported through the Homeowner Benefit Portal at the NYS Tax Department.

The Building Department enforces the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code and the town zoning law. It handles building permits, deck and pool requirements and backflow preventer permits. If you added a deck or pool, ask the department for the permit and inspection record before you list.

Deeds are recorded with the Orange County Clerk. The clerk's office says it will provide a copy of your deed for about $5, and it offers a free alert service that notifies you when a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name, a useful safeguard against deed fraud. The state transfer tax return, Form TP-584, is filed with the county clerk, with payment due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: Is New Windsor a town or a city?
faqs.a: It is a town in Orange County, and the separate city of Newburgh sits along part of its northern line. The Newburgh City School District also covers sections of the town.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying New Windsor property tax late?
faqs.a: One percent in February, then an additional one percent plus a $2.00 notice fee in March. After April 1, unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance.

faqs.q: Does New Windsor have more than one school district?
faqs.a: Yes, four: Newburgh, Washingtonville, Cornwall and Valley Central. The district for your house depends on its address.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a New Windsor home?
faqs.a: With the Orange County Clerk, not Town Hall. The clerk accepts the TP-584 transfer tax form with the deed, and the tax is due within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: How much is the state transfer tax on a New Windsor sale?
faqs.a: It is $2 for every $500 of the price, paid by the seller unless the contract says otherwise. A 1 percent mansion tax applies only to residences of $1 million or more and falls on the buyer.
